newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IG Metall chief warns against EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: German IG Metall chief warns against EMU delay.

text.p: IG Metall chief Klaus Zwickel, head of Germany's largest trade union, on Wednesday warned that a delay in Europe's monetary union would lead to a rise in the mark that would further damage the country's jobs market.
Speaking on the second day of the German trade union federation DGB's jobs conference in Berlin Zwickel nonetheless spoke out against a "Europe for money pushers and currency speculators".

According to the text of a speech made available before delivery, Zwickel saw Europe's planned currency union as a chance to create "a democratic and unified Europe where the current 18 million jobless total could be reduced".
"The deepening of European Union increases the chances to create a European social model to set against world-wide 'Casino capitalism'," Zwickel said.
Zwickel warned against putting too much importance into economic stability policies in the run-up to EMU.

In order to join the currency union, nations face strict entry criteria, including low budget deficits, government debt and stable exchange rates. The currency union is scheduled to be launched on January 1, 1999.
German policy makers have generally favoured a strict interpretation of the entry criteria, arguing that this was necessary to ensure the stability of the new currency, euro.
Zwickel said that such policies run the risk of excluding founding members of European Union from EMU.
"We are for the largest possible number of EMU member countries, from the beginning no EU founding member should be ruled out (of EMU)," Zwickel said.
Zwickel said the Maastricht Treaty did not include any one-sided determination for binding fiscal convergence criteria but added that it did include " a clear determination of labour market goals".
